title: "Exploring flattened data"
output: html_notebook
---

The end product of the flattening process is a new dataset that includes all of the species identifications and metadata associated with each event. We need to take those data and explore them to determine how well the classifications were made.

```{r, results='hide'}
rm(list = ls())
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(magrittr)#allows piping beyond tidyverse
library(googledrive)

myFunctions <-list.files(here("Code", "Functions"), pattern = "R")

#points to files that need to be sourced

invisible(sapply(here("Code", "Functions", myFunctions), source)) #sources all of the functions in the Functions folder.

#invisible function sources the functions without printing value ? and visible FALSE in the console for each function that is sourced.

```

## Pull in data from google drive

### Step 1. Parse the subject data for the entire classification file

#### Load classification file from google drive

Read in data from google drive

```{r}
#entire zooniverse classification file
file_id <- "https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Tm7WiXdknLmmWbPmIv_HRFQYSTFMS30K/view?usp=sharing"
#this pulls north-country-wild-classifications.csv
#need to pass the shared url for the correct csv file here


my_file <- drive_get(file_id) #pulls info from google drive for the file
my_file$name 
#prints file name - check to make sure you have pulled correct file. But first will ask you to authenticate with google drive.

Classified <- read_csv(I(drive_read_string(my_file)))
#may be very slow!

```
Let's clean up and rearrange the data

```{r}
cols_to_drop <- c("subject_ids.y", "user_name.y", "workflow_name.y", "workflow_version.y", "created_at", "metadata", "annotations", "subject_data", "subject." )

Classified <- Classified |>
  select(-all_of(cols_to_drop))
#now rename
 Classified <- Classified |>
   rename(
     subject_ids = subject_ids.x,
     user_name = user_name.x,
     workflow_name = workflow_name.x,
     workflow_version = workflow_version.x
   )

```

And rearrange some columns

```{r}
Classified <- Classified |>
  relocate(c(user_name, workflow_name, workflow_version, task_index, task, task_label, array.index), .after = cam_sd) |>
  relocate(starts_with("subject"), .after = array.index) |>
  relocate(
    starts_with("answers"), .after = cam_sd
  ) |>
  relocate(
    subject_ids, .before = classification_id
  )
```


How many unique subject_ids?
```{r}
Num_subjects<-length(unique(Classified$subject_ids))
```
How many observations per subject_id?
```{r}
Classified |> 
  group_by(subject_ids) |>
  summarise(
    NumClassification = length(choice)) |> 
  arrange(desc(NumClassification)) |>
  View()
```
What is the range in number of classifications per subject id?
```{r}

Classified |>
  group_by(subject_ids) |>
  summarise(NumClassification = length(choice)) |> 
  summary(NumClassification) |>
  View()

```
Plot a histogram of number of classifications
```{r}
PerSubID <- Classified %>% 
  group_by(subject_ids) %>% 
  summarise(NumClassification = length(choice)) |> 
  arrange(desc(NumClassification)) 

ggplot(PerSubID, aes(NumClassification))+
  geom_histogram()
```


Now arrange by subject id
```{r}
Classified<-arrange(Classified, by = subject_ids)
```

Now use this file to begin checking for consensus picks.

Keep in environment and open `Iterative_consensus_picks.qmd`
